_doc: GSSK Household Budget — DETAILED diagram. Every primitive in the model: all counterparties, all accounts, all liabilities, both legs of every physical item, and all four classes of terminal node. Loadable in gssk-dia. See docs/diagrams/household-overview.json for the reduced view.

_ontology.claim: An expense is a boundary transaction with a counterparty, not an edge into a sink. Four distinct expense shapes appear below, and only one of them terminates in a sink directly.
_ontology.1_purchase_to_stock: grocery_buy, toothpaste_buy, fuel_buy — money out, a real thing in, held as household stock. Exchange node couples the two legs at a price.
_ontology.2_purchase_consumed_on_receipt: power_buy, rail_fare — money out, a service in, consumed immediately. The real leg goes straight to heat because that is where it actually goes.
_ontology.3_transfer: ato_tax, lender_interest, insurer_premium, bank_fees — money out, nothing real back. A sink IS correct here, and this is the only class where it is.
_ontology.4_stock_depletion: pantry_stock, toothpaste_stock, car_condition to consumed — no money moves at all. The money was spent at purchase; this is the item being used up.

_terminal_node_classes.boundary: supermarket_revenue, pharmacy_revenue, utility_revenue, fuel_co_revenue, rail_revenue — money that crossed the household boundary. Conserved, still exists, now in someone else's system. Modelled as a sink because the household's frame ends here, NOT because the money was destroyed.
_terminal_node_classes.transfer: ato_tax, lender_interest, insurer_premium, bank_fees — as above, but with no real counter-flow.
_terminal_node_classes.accounting: value_lost — book value written down. No counterparty, no physical referent, no conservation claim.
_terminal_node_classes.dissipation: heat — Odum's heat sink. The only thermodynamically terminal node in the model.
_terminal_node_classes.depletion: consumed — material used up by the household.

_omitted.toothpaste_reorder_switch: REQ-RENEW-1's switch-gated repurchase is deliberately absent. The switch node's gating semantics are not pinned by a golden-vector test yet, and drawing a wire whose behaviour is unverified would put a claim in the diagram that the kernel may not honour. Tracked as task d1-pin-switch-gain-semantics.
_omitted.offset_feedback: The offset account does not yet modulate mortgage interest. This is REQ-MDL-8's deliberate omission: it is the feedback edge the calibration and structure-search machinery is meant to discover, not one the author asserts.

metadata.name: Household Budget — Detailed
metadata.description: Full household budget network. Expenses are exchange-node boundary transactions with named counterparties; terminal nodes are separated into boundary crossings, transfers, accounting write-downs, material depletion and genuine dissipation.
metadata.author: gssk-budget

carriers._note: Declared but carrying no flows yet (REQ-MDL-5). The hook for advice, alerts and decisions, held back deliberately under REQ-HON-3.

nodes._class: LIABILITY — debt counter on the money carrier, not a money holding
TRANSACTION DIAMOND — service consumed on receipt
TRANSACTION DIAMOND — service consumed on receipt
ASSET — durable, PHYSICAL leg (REQ-ONT-1). A car whose book value is zero still exists and still costs money to run.
TRANSFER SINK — money out, nothing real back
BOUNDARY SINK — money crossed into the counterparty's system
ACCOUNTING SINK — book value written down, no counterparty
DISSIPATION SINK — Odum's heat sink, the only thermodynamically terminal node

edges._note: Fortnightly salary as a forcing waveform (REQ-TIME-2). phase is a TIME offset in days, SUBTRACTED (REQ-TIME-4).
Employer superannuation contribution.
Rent received enters through the income_asset yield gate.
Yield gate delivers rent to the account.
Discretionary transfer to the goal buffer. Linear: saving scales with what is available.
Transfer to offset. The offset does not yet modulate mortgage interest — see _omitted.offset_feedback.
Mortgage interest accrual. REQ-FLOW-2: pinned constant as origin, interaction logic, principal as control_node. control_node is read, never consumed.
Principal repayment drains the debt counter. threshold floors it at zero.
TRANSFER — the cash leg of the mortgage repayment actually leaving the account.
Credit card interest, same pinned-origin interaction pattern.
Card principal repayment drains the debt counter.
TRANSFER — cash leg of the card repayment.
TRANSFER — income tax. Money out, nothing real back. A sink is correct here.
TRANSFER — insurance premium. Nothing real flows back until a claim, which is an event, not a rate.
TRANSFER — account keeping fees.
PURCHASE TO STOCK — groceries. Money leg in.
Goods leg in — the supermarket supplies the transaction.
Goods leg out — groceries become household stock. This is the leg a money-only expense model discards.
Money leg out — payment crosses the boundary into the supermarket's system. F_money = price x F_goods.
STOCK DEPLETION — no money moves. Linear: use proportional to stock on hand.
PURCHASE TO STOCK — toothpaste. Money leg in.
Goods leg in.
Goods leg out — a tube enters stock.
Money leg out — crosses the boundary.
STOCK DEPLETION — constant use, 1 tube per 42 days. The purchase price was expensed the day it was bought; this flow is the tube being used, and no money moves.
SERVICE CONSUMED ON RECEIPT — electricity. Money leg in.
Energy leg in — the retailer supplies the transaction.
Energy leg out — there is no household stock of grid electricity, so it goes straight to genuine dissipation.
Money leg out — the bill crosses the boundary.
PURCHASE TO STOCK — fuel. Money leg in.
Energy leg in.
Energy leg out — fuel is stored, unlike electricity.
Money leg out — crosses the boundary.
Fuel burned. Genuine dissipation.
SERVICE CONSUMED ON RECEIPT — rail fare. Money leg in.
Transport work in — the operator supplies it.
Transport work out — consumed on the journey and dissipated. Nothing enters household stock.
Money leg out — crosses the boundary into the operator's system.
ACCOUNTING — declining-balance depreciation of the car's money leg (REQ-FLOW-1 default).
PHYSICAL — the car's condition leg degrading. Deliberately a different rate from the money leg: book value falls faster than the machine wears out, which is exactly why REQ-ONT-1 keeps them apart.
ACCOUNTING — rental property depreciation.
